title: Onboarding hardening: domain attestations, denylist propagation, and admin controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current org/team onboarding allows account creation and team joins that bypass a single, auditable domain verification step. This leads to: 1) inconsistent enforcement of allowlist/denylist rules across SSO and email-based invites, 2) gaps in audit logs for domain-assertion changes, and 3) unclear admin controls for scoped auto-accept (e.g., auto-accept whitelisted domains vs manual approval).

Goal: Implement an admin-facing set of controls and runtime enforcement that: (a) centralizes domain attestation state (verified / pending / revoked) tied to org metadata, (b) ensures allowlist/denylist propagation across invite flows and SAML provisioning, (c) surfaces domain changes in audit logs with enough context for post-incident forensics, and (d) provides a safe migration path to RBAC v2 with minimal customer disruption.

Scope:
- Backend: domain attestation model and APIs; denylist/allowlist evaluation service that runs during invite, SAML SCIM provisioning, and magic-link/email join flows; event hooks to record domain events to audit log store.
- Console: admin UI to view/verify domains, mark domains as org-verified, configure auto-accept policies per team, and a propagation dashboard for denylist updates.
- Integrations: SAML provisioning paths must consult the same central service; SCIM mappings should carry domain assertion metadata.
- Observability: new Grafana panels and ELK queries to monitor invite failures due to denylist and frequency of domain verification changes.

Non-goals: changes to external identity providers themselves; building an identity proofing system (we rely on existing DNS TXT or SAML-based attestations).
comments: 2026-02-11 - Design review with Claire Nguyen: agreed to represent domain attestation as a first-class org object rather than ad-hoc flags on invites. Design will include audit_reason and verified_by fields. Action: PM to draft UI copy (PM-412).

2026-02-13 - Security sync: cryptographic signing of attestation records is optional for this phase; we'll rely on stored events + KMS-backed audit log for tamper-evidence. Security requested an explicit retention policy for domain events.

2026-02-15 - Engineering note: prototype service returned for allowlist check via gRPC with 2ms median latency in local perf tests. We will add a LRU cache for domain verdicts to avoid SLO regressions.
2026-02-16 - Dependency update: waiting on ENG-82111 (RBAC v2 role mapping) to expose 'org-admin.can_manage_domains' permission before admin UI can be gated.

2026-02-18 - UX feedback from PM: admin should be able to bulk-revoke a domain and schedule a rollout window for auto-rejecting joins to avoid immediate disruption. Added 'scheduled_action' metadata to the plan.
2026-02-19 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1478 - adds domain-attestation model + allowlist service and unit tests. Needs integration tests and canary rollout plan.
